about: argv[0]'s basename selects a subcommand when the spec declares multicall. clap's busybox-style applets: the dispatcher names (name and bin) are skipped, any other basename is the first word, and a trailing .exe plus path components are stripped so /usr/bin/ls and ls.exe select the same applet.

vectors.doc: A symlink invocation: argv[0]'s basename is the applet, and the rest of argv belongs to it.
vectors.spec:
name "busybox"
bin "busybox"
multicall #true
cmd "ls" {
  arg "[ARGS]..."
}
cmd "cat"

vectors.doc: A dispatcher invocation still skips argv[0], so busybox ls is the ls applet.
A trailing .exe is stripped so Windows and Unix agree on the applet name.
An unknown applet is the same error as an unmatched word: nothing can hold it.
An unknown applet is forwarded when the root declares external_subcommand, including flags after it.
vectors.spec:
name "busybox"
bin "busybox"
multicall #true
unknown_flags "error"
external_subcommand #true
cmd "ls"

vectors.doc: Either dispatcher name skips argv[0]: `bin` matching is enough even when `name` differs.
An unknown applet is an unmatched word, so default_subcommand still catches it.
vectors.spec:
name "busybox"
bin "busybox"
multicall #true
default_subcommand "ls"
cmd "ls" {
  arg "[ARGS]..."
}

vectors.doc: Invoking the dispatcher with no further words stays at the root; it does not invent an applet.
